origin.description: Secant search on the initial slope of a second-order equation so the end condition is zero. Each trial is integrated with ode45.
origin.usage: shooting(f, t0, tfinal, y0, h, a, b, itermax = 20, tol = 1e-6, hmax = 0)

arguments.name: f
arguments.text: Second derivative y'' = f(t, y, y').

arguments.name: t0
arguments.text: Start of the interval.

arguments.name: tfinal
arguments.text: End of the interval.

arguments.name: y0
arguments.text: Initial value, not the initial slope.

arguments.name: h
arguments.text: End condition h(y, y') = 0.

arguments.name: a
arguments.text: First guess of the initial slope.

arguments.name: b
arguments.text: Second guess of the initial slope.

arguments.name: itermax
arguments.text: Maximum secant iterations.

arguments.name: tol
arguments.text: Stop when the end condition is this small, and pass it to ode45.

arguments.name: hmax
arguments.text: Maximum ode45 step. 0 uses that solver's default.

origin.details: y'' = -y, y(0) = 1, y(0.5) = cos(0.5), with slope guesses 0 and -1. The check vector is the solution, column by column.
origin.value: Secant search on the initial slope of a second-order equation so the end condition is zero. Each trial is integrated with ode45.
origin.example: print(c(shooting(function(t, y1, y2) -y1, 0, 0.5, 1, function(u, v) u - cos(0.5), 0, -1, tol=1e-6, hmax=0.1)$y))
